message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What Happens | |---------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you agree on). Points are earned by being the first to finish each round. | | **Setup** | • 108‑card deck (standard Uno).
• Each player draws 7 cards.
• Place the remaining deck face‑down as the draw pile.
• Turn the top card of the draw pile face‑up to start the discard pile. | | **Turn Order** | Clockwise (unless a reverse card is played). | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play one card that matches the **color**, **number**, or **symbol** of the top discard.
• If you have no playable card, you must draw from the draw pile.
• If the drawn card is playable, you may play it immediately. | | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes direction of play.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses a turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses a turn (must be played only if you have no matching color). | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you play your second‑to‑last card, shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The first player to discard all their cards wins the round. | | **Scoring** | Add up the point values of the cards left in opponents’ hands:
• Number cards = face value.
• Draw Two, Reverse, Skip = 20 points each.
• Wild, Wild Draw Four = 50 points each.
Winner’s score = sum of opponents’ points. | | **Game End** | First player to reach the agreed‑upon score (e.g., 500) wins the game. | **Optional Variations** | Variation | How It Changes the Game | |-----------|------------------------| | **Stacking** | Players may stack Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards instead of drawing. | | **No Wild Draw Four** | Some groups prefer to remove this card entirely. | | **Custom Decks** | Use themed decks (e.g., Uno with custom colors or symbols). | **Quick Tips** 1. Keep an eye on the discard pile to anticipate what cards opponents might need. 2. Use Wild cards strategically to change the color when you’re stuck. 3. Remember to call “UNO” loudly—no one likes a surprise penalty! Enjoy your game!
